articleTitle: Log periodic microstrip array
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: This paper represents the results of log periodic microstrip antenna design for octave frequency band 8-18 GHz. Such an antenna was invented by P.S. Hall (1986), the main advantages of this antenna are: good size-weight characteristics; ability of conformable mounting on curved surfaces; and relatively low cost and high reliability of parameters due to modern microwave printed circuit technology of manufacturing. The main technical requirements for antenna under design are: beamwidth of radiation pattern in azimuth plane 90 deg., in elevation plane 30 deg.; mainlobe direction due to the axis of cylindrical carrier 90 deg.; input VSWR 2-2.5 in frequency band 8-18 GHz; and antenna gain 9-10 dB. The electromagnetically coupled rectangular microstrip patch had been used as radiating element of array.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave band-pass filter using active matching principles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: A MMIC band-pass active filter at Ka-band using active matching devices have been successfully implemented employing 0.2 /spl mu/m-GaAs P-HEMT technology. A 5% measured relative bandwidth at millimeter frequencies have been achieved and validates the accuracy of the design methodology. In this contribution measured results have been reported with prime attention to low noise figure and power performance as it is necessary at the input of a receiver.

articleTitle: On the matching of micro-wave irradiator with hydrogen containing media
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The slot irradiator fabricated on the lateral surface of the thin wall metallic tube is considered. The equivalent circuit of the slot irradiator is proposed and its characteristics and parameters for matching with media having loss are determined. Comparison with the experimental data for the tubes of various diameters in the frequency range 0.85-1.1 GHz is presented.

articleTitle: Optimization of varactor tunable microstrip resonators for wireless applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: This paper presents analysis, optimization and performance of stepped varactor tunable microstrip resonator (S-VTMR) using proper circuit models. The general form of resonance conditions tuning facilities of these configurations and higher harmonics behaviour are investigated. Based on the new optimization algorithm, coupling elements stabilizing a bandwidth have been suggested. The experimental S-VTMR with series varactor circuits has been fabricated and tested demonstrating a good agreement with the circuit model predictions.

articleTitle: New structures of controllable attenuators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The new practical circuits of the electrical controllable diode attenuator have been developed. The characteristic feature of attenuators is very small phase shift at smooth regulation of the transfer factor. It is shown, that use of the correction circuits leads to essential reduction of the phase shift. For picosecond attenuators the phase stability of 1-5 degrees in working frequency band up to 2 GHz and attenuation range up to 25 dB is achieved.

articleTitle: Optimization of arbitrary frequency response of microwave bandstop filter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The optimization tool developed consists of a combination of evolution strategy with genetic algorithms. The improved algorithm proved it's capability in optimizing a microwave filter application with arbitrary frequency response. The optimization tool is especially tolerant to input parameter definitions and is efficiently capable of overcoming local optima. The algorithm was developed under the constraint of rapid convergence speed which was increased by more than one order of magnitude compared to the evolution-strategy-alone procedure. The developed optimization tool can be applied to a variety of technical problems, where the performance of a technical device has to meet given specifications, and where this performance is defined numerically by the parameters of the device to be optimized.

articleTitle: Artificial neural networks for planar waveguide junctions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In recent years, artificial neural networks (ANNs) have been introduced as fast and accurate tools for modeling simulating and optimizing a great variety of microwave structures. In this paper we propose a multilayer perceptron neural network (MLPNN) for modelling planar waveguide junctions involving waveguides with arbitrary shapes and with variable geometrical features. The artificial neural network has been used to represent the modal spectrum of the arbitrary waveguides, and the coupling-integrals between such waveguides and standard rectangular waveguides, as a function of the variable geometrical feature(s). The training data set has been obtained,using an accurate but slow electromagnetic simulation algorithm. The result obtained is shown to be a very accurate and extremely, efficient representation of the waveguide junction.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental implementation of microwave active filters using automatic frequency control techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The paper discusses phase locked loop (PLL) and magnitude locked loop (MLL) techniques based on voltage controlled filter (VCF), for the automatic frequency control (AFC) of active filters. Applications to a microwave planar filter are considered. Theoretical analysis, simulated and measured results are presented for both phase and magnitude control circuits enabling the filter to accurately track a reference signal.

articleTitle: Analysis of the transmission strip lines with the "LINES DESIGNER" package for Windows
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The program package LINES DESIGNER 1.1 intended for calculation of distributed parameters of the transmission strip lines is developed for various types of lines such as single and multiconductor lines. The existing package version 1.1 supports 26 types of strip lines and allows carrying out calculation of all parameters, which are needed for subsequent circuit-analysis of the microwave devices. There are two design modes. The first mode is one with fixed parameter values, and the second mode is one with varied line parameters in a desired range. The design results are presented as either a numerical table or graphic plots. There is also an opportunity to generate a design report. The quasi-static analysis based on a novel algorithm, which combines a method of enclosed subregions with conformal mapping technique, is used for calculation of the the stripline parameters. Some results of numerical modeling in comparison with known ones are submitted. The package LINES DESIGNER 1.1 is intended for use in Windows 95/98/NT. There is also a DOS version.

articleTitle: Thin-film comb thermal converter: influence of shunt effect of thermopile on high-frequency current distribution
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Thin-film comb thermal converters are widely used for obtaining mean square values of alternating current or voltage and for measuring a power of electrical signals having various forms. At the present time reliable data about the operation of these thermal converters on high-frequencies are absent. In this paper the analytical model allowing one to determine the influence of the shunt effect of the thermopile on the high frequency current distribution in the structure of the thin-film comb thermal converter is presented. The structure of the thin-film comb thermal converter under consideration is shown. In this structure hot thermojunctions of the thermopile are placed near the heater. Such disposition of the hot thermojunctions permits the value of the operation frequency of the thermal converter to be increased to 500 to 600 MHz.

articleTitle: High purity AlGaAs grown by molecular beam epitaxy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: We report the growth and photoluminescence of very high quality Al/sub x/Ga/sub 1-x/As layers grown by molecular beam epitaxy over the 0<x<0.38 composition range. Heterostructure doped-channel FETs manufactured on pseudomorphic AlGaAs/InGaAs/GaAs heterostructures containing this layer have output power of about 1 W/mm with 7.8 dB gain and 60% power-added efficiency at 18 GHz.

articleTitle: An improved approach for resonant measurements of complex permittivity of lossy liquids
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: An improved approach for evaluation of complex permittivity of liquids using a cylindrical microwave cavity at E/sub 010/ natural mode is presented. Evaluation is processed on the basis of measured electrical parameters of the cavity with a sample inserted into centered glass tube. The approach is based on the consideration of forced oscillations boundary problem for the cavity coupled to a measuring microwave circuit. Numerical evaluation of characteristic equation for the natural mode is used. Ohmic losses in cavity walls are taken into account in the field model employed. There is no limitations in permittivity and loss tangent values of materials measured. Comparison of complex permittivity values given by the approach being presented with ones given by the simple perturbation approach conventionally adopted in resonant measurements is done.

articleTitle: The mathematical model of the active two-port for broadband microwave amplifier with the feedback parallel dipole
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: A model of the active four-port for the wideband UHF amplifier cascade on the basis of given gain, reflecting and structure of two-port section of the parallel feedback is described.

articleTitle: An analytical description of the Greek cross as a piezotransducer with the aid of z/sub ij/ resistances
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: This paper is devoted to the problem of analytical description of the Greek cross as piezotransducer with the aid of z/sub ij/ resistances. An analytical view of the matrix of z/sub ij/ resistances for Greek cross is obtained. An experimental investigation of the Greek cross-shaped piezoresistive element is hold. Very good accordance between theory and experiment is observed.

articleTitle: Cell of the waveguide band-pass filter with poles of attenuation on finite frequencies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Waveguide band-pass filters with cavity have high characteristic stability and small losses; however, the dimensions and weight of such filters are too big. As a rule, it is polynomial filters with direct coupled cavity or more seldom with quarter-wave coupled ones. In such filters all zeros are located in a passband, and the poles are on a zero frequency and in infinity. The greater selectivity can be achieved if the frequencies of these poles are given the finite values. Frequently in practice, the monotonous increasing of attenuation in stop-band is not required, and the distribution of poles by Butterworth or Chebyshev is not effective, and filters have superfluous electrical and constructive characteristics. A band-pass section is described.

articleTitle: Design method and optimization of noise performances for different types of planar microwave active filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In this paper, we study the optimization of noise performance for two types of planar microwaves active filters. This kind of filter uses MMIC active circuit loss compensation of planar microstrip resonators. We use the noise wave formalism to calculate the analytical expression of the noise factors. Simulated and measured results are presented to validate our study and can be extended to various other possible planar topologies.

articleTitle: The step-down transformer on lines having an arbitrary ratio of transformation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The new type of step-down transformer is offered. The transformer does not demand the ferrite core and can be designed with an arbitrary ratio of transformation proportional to a whole number and to a broken number more than one in any case. The transformer may be used as the matching network or its part for the broad-band transistor power amplifiers.

articleTitle: 0.4 watt X-band quasimonolithic amplifier-design, results, comparative analysis of simulating methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The development of the new X-band electronics systems needs amplifiers with output power of 0.3-0.4 W, reliable, not so costly, with small weight and dimensions. This paper concerns design and measured characteristics of experimental quasimonolithic amplifier (QMAMP) with the output power of 0.4 W and the power gain of 12-16 dB in the frequency band 9-12 GHz, and gives comparative analysis of the results of using the small signal S-parameters and the time domain large signal approaches in the design of GaAs power amplifiers.

articleTitle: Nonlinear distortions in passive varactor tunable resonators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: It is considered the estimation of nonlinear distortions for tunable filters based on passive resonators consists of uniform transmission line sections and varactors. By using nonlinear analysis of different configuration of filters it is shown that filters with the connection of varactors in series have much larger spurious free dynamic region as compared with schematic filters with varactor connection in parallel.

articleTitle: Systems for generating AC power of the "generator-AC-DC voltage source converter-DC-AC voltage source converter" type
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: A generating system of the "generator-AC-DC voltage source converter-DC-AC voltage source converter" type, with the generator having the unity power factor is presented and a new AC-DC converter control algorithm is proposed. A possibility for application to an induction machine as a generator is approached.

articleTitle: Development of the automated measurement system for identification of multidimensional transfer functions of nonlinear devices at multitone test signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Offers the modified block diagram of multidimensional transfer functions (MTF) meter in which one considerable magnification of an exactitude of measurements of MTF can be obtained as a result of minimization of a peak-factor of a multitone measuring signal. The wideband ideal /spl pi//2-phasor of heterodyne channel is changed by a simple nondispersing delay line with arbitrary phase shift.

articleTitle: Physiotherapeutic devices of optic and Ehf-band waves
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Low-intensive radiation of visible, infra-red and EHF-band wave is widely used in medicine as non-invasive methods of treatment. Different models of medical devices in the specified range are developed and are mass-produced. They are clinically tested and have proved their efficiency. The absence of side-effects, considerable reduction in treatment time serves as impetus to research and development of move modern physiotherapeutic devices. This report describes new research and development for the results of optic and EHF-band wave devices.

articleTitle: Low-dimensional model of a microwave resonator with p-n junction varactor diode
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In many microwave devices there are units involving a length of transmission line and a semiconductor element with p-n junction. These systems can operate separately (for example, as a resonant filter returned by a varactor) or be a part of a circuit (in some generators a section of the line is inserted between the transistor base and collector). In general such units can be considered as distributed systems with the lumped nonlinearity. The experiments with various transmission lines with silicon varactor diodes have shown, that at high power of external periodic excitation these systems demonstrate a hierarchy of periodic, quasiperiodic and chaotic oscillations. Various scenarios of transition to chaos are observed, and namely via a cascade of period doubling bifurcations, intermittency and collapse of torus. A low-dimensional model has been constructed, qualitatively representing the parameter space structure of the distributed system. The purpose of the present paper is to investigate the influence of the varactor diode location on the dynamics of a driven microwave resonator and to model this situation with nonautonomous circuits.

articleTitle: Several applications of MMIC negative resistance topologies for microwave bandstop and bandpass filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: This paper presents a method to synthesize microwave active filters using negative resistances in MMIC technology. The negative resistance circuits employed are based on classical negative impedance converters (NICs). Our topologies are validated with computer simulations and with measurements. We then associate our circuits with several microwave bandstop and bandpass filters.

articleTitle: Actively compensated planar ring resonator structures suitable for bandstop and bandpass filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In this paper the design of bandstop and bandpass filters is studied by means of algebraic manipulations using theory of recursive filters. The objective of these analytical investigations on recursive type functions is to find novel topologies suitable for frequency tuneable bandstop or bandpass responses using only coupled planar ring resonators and amplifiers. We show how the noise factor of this category of filters can be analytically derived and effectively minimized by using appropriate unbalanced power couplers and amplifiers. We validate our approach with simulated examples for each topology.

articleTitle: Waveguide bandstop filter with direct relationships
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In traditional waveguide bandstop filters resonators are spread at a distance of 3/spl lambda//sub g//4. Resonators are usually implemented in the form of series stubs (in E-plane). Under relaxed requirements for the steepness of the frequency response, it is possible to build filters on resonant circuits with direct coupling. Resonance probes are placed in reference planes of the E-junction. Experience shows, with such a joint at the expense of the additional coupling, the equivalent Q-factor of the stubs and especially the probes is decreased. For reducing this relationship it is possible to use diaphragms or a stub with a smaller waveguide cross-section.

articleTitle: Calculation likelihood for cyclical codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The expression for determination of likely ratio (l.r.) for the group code was represented by Ahuvalov et al. (1993). For calculation of the l.r. it is necessary to define the weight numerator, corresponding to the error combination. This paper finds formulas for calculation of weight numerator for cyclical codes.

articleTitle: Volumetric integral equations for non-uniform impurities in the rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Surface Integral Equations (SIEs) and Volumetric Integral Equations (VIEs) are widely used for solutions of electromagnetic boundary problems. The SIEs are convenient because they reduce the dimension of a problem (three-dimensional problems are reduced to two-dimensional SIEs) and allow all boundary and radiating conditions to be satisfied. Both the SIEs with the kernels as single- and double-layered potentials and the VIEs versus the electrical field distribution in the volume of an impurity, are known and have been used. In this paper the VIEs without surface integrals are developed for arbitrary dielectric and magnetic inclusions in the Rectangular Waveguide (RW). The goal of the paper is to elaborate the algorithms for solutions of boundary problems with arbitrary shaped inclusions and with arbitrary tensor permittivities and permeabilities (including bianisotropic ones). The method is based on piece-wise field approximations.

articleTitle: A method for characterizing resistive and dielectric materials in VHF using the detection by integration principle
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: This paper describes a simple and new process for characterization of resistive and dielectric materials in VHF range. We have developed a computer program which permits to simulate the analogical function used in detection by integration measurement. The obtained results show a good measurement accuracy comparing to the analogical method.

articleTitle: Gas discharger generators of ultra-frequency a metal-bearing plasma to etching of piezoelectrics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The etching of lithium niobate in a high-voltage glow discharge with voltage of 10 KV is discussed. Pulsed supply of metal vapors into the etching chamber causes the discharge resignation and the generation of high frequency oscillations. An inductive-capacitate composition in a discharge circuit generates frequency 5 MHz. This helps to remove discharge from the piezoelectric surface and to increase the etching speed to 5 mcm/h.

articleTitle: Software for designing of dipole antenna arrays, multi-frequency matching with wide-band antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: As analysis can show, in present time software for designing of dipole antennas and antenna arrays, assembled from such antennas is not available. Existing means (program YagiMax, NEC-2, NECLFWIN, NEC4WIN95 and other) does not provide all the necessary capabilities. In RSTU the advanced programs for this goals have been developed. They are Uda-Yagi and AntArray programs. Both of them works under Windows 95/98/NT.

articleTitle: Optimization of high-voltage RF power SiGe transistors for cellular applications [HBTs]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The base profile design for high-voltage RF power silicon transistors with epitaxial SiGe base was studied using 2-D process and device simulations. The addition of Ge in the base makes thin base widths with very high base doping possible. This gives rise to a higher maximum oscillation frequency thus improving the critical power gain for these devices.

articleTitle: Design features for high pressure transducers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In this experimental work the polysilicon pressure transducers are designed with pressure-sensitive elements and made for pressures over 5 MPa. To determine the magnitude of mechanical stress in the diaphragm, we defined gauge factors from longitudinal and transverse piezoresistors on the console beam made from the same wafer as the diaphragm. Also, we made a model for mechanical stress in the diaphragm by the finite element method (FEM) by taking into account not only the uniformly distributed load on the plate of the diaphragm, but also the load on the lateral side of the diaphragm. The comparison of the calculated mechanical stress with the experimentally defined one has shown a coincidence within 20% error bound.

articleTitle: Using relative compensatory method in adaptive filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The realization in temporary and frequency of algorithms of work of adaptive filters requires plenty of operations of multiplication. However construction of similar equalisers can be essentially simplified, using for these purposes controlled digital filters. Thus the characteristics of such algorithms not only concede the similar characteristics of adaptive digital filters, but even surpass them. The essence of the offered method is the use of the principle of a relativity for construction of similar equalisers. The use of properties of a relativity for creation of such equalisers is named by the author the relative compensatory method.

articleTitle: Measurement of S-parameters of microwave multiport network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: On the basis of measurement scattering matrix of six-port network by triple six-port network analyzer the algorithm determination of S-parameter microwave multiport network was exploited.

articleTitle: Calculation of harmonics level in microwave varactor mixer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Varactor mixers are used as converters in transmitters. Energy calculation of powerful varactor converters of frequency is designed sufficiently well. On the mixer two signals are given-carrier frequency and modulating frequency.

articleTitle: The simulation of charge transport phenomena in heterostructures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: A program for modeling structures containing sharp and smooth heterojunctions is created. The account in the program is conducted in view of Fermi-Dirac statistics. Diffusion and carrier charge drift are taken into account. With the help of this program the HEMT structure was simulated and the I-V characteristics of this structure were designed.

articleTitle: Calculation of combinational frequency level in microwave varactor mixer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Gives the calculation of the harmonic level of the lowest of mixed frequencies in a summary varactor mixer. By the analysis of combinational components we use a method of directed graphs, as was made for the calculation of the harmonic.

articleTitle: Fiber-optical transducers of mechanical quantities
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The paper treats construction principles, design solutions and research characteristics of mechanical quantities fiber optical transducers (FOT).

articleTitle: Rydberg's sodium atoms as high-sensitive narrowband reconfigurable microwave detector
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: An interaction of microwave radiation with high-excited (Rydberg) atoms has been suggested to be used for radiation detection and measurement of its frequency. Our objective in the present work was to investigate experimentally and theoretically the spectrum of the microwave transition 37P-37S in sodium Rydberg atoms in a weak static electric field and to perform accurate measurements of the scalar and tensor polarizabilities of the 37P level. Knowledge of polarizabilities is required to find a magnitude of energy level shifts in atom by known static electric fields. The Na S and P states possess large quantum defects (1.347 and 0.854, respectively), so that a quadratic Stark effect in weak fields is characteristic for these levels.

articleTitle: The problem of estimation of mechanical stresses and deformation calculation of its solution with FEM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The author attempts to develop an analytical model for calculation of strain in the area near stress concentrators in elastic elements, using a finite element method implemented in a CAD system.

articleTitle: Distribution of zeros and poles in multiplying tubes of frequencies on non-regular lines of transmission
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The task of suppression of all stray passbands of bandpass filters used in multiplying tubes of frequency is decided. The effect of suppression is carried out at the expense of compensation of resonance frequencies. The analytical expressions for synthesis of such filters are obtained.

articleTitle: Generalized link of parameter sets for linear and "reduced to linear" systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The simple formula linking any sets of matrices of parameters for linear and nonlinear "reduced to linear" systems is obtained. On simple examples, the obtained results for deriving any of the possible matrices of parameters is shown. The outcomes of the work essentially simplify deriving of the matrices of parameters, since any matrix of parameters of reduced to linear systems can be primarily obtained from any other by using the same formula. The outcomes can be used in any areas, where models of this kind of matrix parameter are used, and particularly, in tasks of linear circuit analysis, and as a basis for building up the theory of nonlinear systems without memory-"reduced to linear" systems.

articleTitle: Application of autodyne ehf-band sensor for transport electronics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Multifunctional (autodyne) application of Gunn diodes allows to considerably simplify the schematic and design representation of devices. It means that the transmitter and transformer functions are provided at the same time with the amplification of useful.

articleTitle: A computation of H-plane waveguide circulator by a finite element method
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In the article the computation of main characteristics of ferrite Y-circulator by finite element method is presented.

articleTitle: Integral equations for nonlinear structures of electrodynamics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In recent times there have been many investigations and uses of electromagnetic structures (ES) with nonlinear media and devices. The simplest electrodynamic model for a nonlinear device is the introduction of nonlinear boundary conditions. The linear composite (or complex) anisotropic and bianisotropic media present another field of interest. As these media may be nonlinear, it it interesting to develop the model which describes all these cases. This is the goal of the paper, which is achieved using the integral equation.

articleTitle: Classical and tuneable band-pass filters using MMIC negative resistance circuits for losses compensation and size reduction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: New band-pass filter design techniques are presented using classical passive interdigitated filters. An MMIC active component circuit assists all the filter designs. The MMIC component performs a negative resistance with an associated imaginary part. By using this component, the negative resistance leads to compensation for the losses of the passive filter while the imaginary part leads to reduction of the length of the resonator. Two filters, implemented in microstrip and coplanar technologies, have been designed and tested to demonstrate our approach. In the last step, we have developed a frequency tuneable band-pass filter.

articleTitle: Gas chromatography investigations of the adsorbents in the microwave-field
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The installation designed for the microwave-exposure adsorbents with the purpose of the modification of their chromatography properties is represented in this communication. The results of the retention data investigations have been obtained during the variation of both the frequency and power microwave-oscillation and the temperature as well.

articleTitle: Design, analysis and optimization of varactor tunable microstrip filter for wireless applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: This paper presents design, analysis, optimization and performance of a varactor tunable microstrip filter (VTMF) using proper circuit models. Based on the optimization algorithm, coupling elements stabilizing the bandwidth have been suggested. The experimental sample VTMF with series varactor circuits have been fabricated and tested, demonstrating a good agreement with the circuit model predictions.

articleTitle: To a problem adaptation of two-signal analyzers of microwave circuit
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The common principle of the amplitude and the phase adaptation of two-signal analyzer of microwave circuit is formulated. The introducing into consideration unconditional adaptation allows to decide the actual problem of the actual measurement complex reflection coefficient.

articleTitle: Multi-frequency matching for wide-band antennas
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: For matching of complex load with transmission line two cases are usually examined: narrow-band and wide-band matching. However in practice often it is necessary to ensure two-frequency or multi-frequency matching, when ideal matching on two or several narrow frequency bands is required. The authors examine the two-frequency matching method. This method allows matching of arbitrary complex loads on two arbitrary frequencies. The method is based on L-type circuit usage. Matching network structure is shown. On one frequency first L-circuit L1 or L2 matches load with transmission line. On the second frequency input impedances of these L-circuits are Z/sub L1/ and Z(L2). The second L-circuit matches these impedances with the line on second frequency. Then the elements of the second L-circuit are replaced by parallel and serial oscillating contours. Resonance is present on the first frequency and the first L-circuit does not affect the whole network; on the second frequency contour impedances are equal to respective L-circuit elements impedance. The resulted network provides two-frequency matching.

articleTitle: Cascade section in waveguide
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The author analyses a cascade section in a waveguide and relates this to the design of a filter with a passband cascade section. It is pointed out that the cascading of passband sections allows a perfect frequency response to be obtained.

articleTitle: Noise properties of second order microstrip active filter with negative resistance compensation for a loss
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: A second order microstrip active filter is considered. A single negative resistance element is used to achieve compensation for the loss of two resonators of the filter. The negative resistance element is implemented using the optimization of FET feedback circuits for noise reduction. A comparison with the same bandwidth passive filter is presented.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic models of biconical, TEM-horn type antenna
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The increase of interest in broadband antennas is connected with the expansion of frequency range of satellite communication systems. The object of our research is a broadband antenna of quasi-pyramidal horn type without side walls (T-horn). The given antenna may be used in the capacity of excitation source of a parabolic antenna or in the capacity of an antenna array element. The basic excited wave for such an antenna is TEM-wave. We examine two independent models of the antenna. The first is static, it is based on idea of TEM-horn as a part of infinite biconical line with current distribution and follows the travelling wave law. The second model is based on spectral presentation of electromagnetic field when solving integral equation for boundary problem.

articleTitle: The phase shift measurer on the basis of multipliers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: At the Department of Theoretical Fundamentals of Radio Engineering, sonar systems to identify the location and the structure of underwater objects (UO) have been designed and developed. In the systems, by comparison with the traditional ones, additional information from the UO is obtained by means of measuring the phase frequency response of the UO. In order to realize the new method multicomponent phase-tied signals are emitted and a phase shift between the components of the echo signals is measured. In order to reduce the weight and the dimensions of the equipment, parametrical emitting antennas instead of traditional ones are offered for use. The emitting element is fed with a multicomponent phase-tied signal with high frequency (in the millimeter frequency range). As a result of the nonlinear interaction of the high frequency components in the water, harmonics of the waves with a frequency difference between them are formed, i.e., a multicomponent phase-tied waves. In order to measure the reflection phase-frequency response of an UO in a wide frequency band one must vary the frequencies F and 2F of the signals and filter the waves. In the receivers of the systems phase shift measurers (PSM) are applied. Two amplifiers with double frequency conversion and highly selective elements filter the waves with frequencies F and 2F. The realization of the receiver and the PSM has many difficulties. Therefore another realization of the units is developed which does not contain highly-selective elements.

articleTitle: Broadband-wideangle phase shifter for stochastic cooling in heavy-ion accelerator facility
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: This paper describes design and performance of a broadband-wideangle phase shifter developed for a special application. Three identical phase shifters are implemented in a control-loop circuit within a stochastic-cooling system to generate very thin, high precision heavy-ion beams. The loop design requests wide-angle phase range, wide frequency band, and controllable phase constant with frequency. Precision ion beams are very promising for research in particle physics and may be used in the future for cancer treatment also.

articleTitle: The estimation method for the inductance of high T/sub c/ interferometer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The results of the inductance estimation of a bulk high T/sub c/ interferometer of Zimmerman-type are presented. The estimation was obtained by the analysis of peak-frequency characteristic of the interferometer and output characteristics of the RF SQUID-magnetometer.

articleTitle: Optimal frequency in acoustic location
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The choice of operating frequency in acoustic location is highly problematic and is found by compromise. From the one side, the frequency should be as higher as possible so that to achieve the high accuracy and directivity. From the other side, the lower is the frequency, the weaker are oscillations in the medium and the more is the sonar range, the lower is the thermal noise level. In this paper the optimal frequency for location in a water medium is found in a marine and river medium. As an optimal criterion for defining f/sub opt/ we took the ratio of intensity of echo signal to the sum of noise intensity and reverberation. We received a general ratio and formulas for typical instances.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Shubnikov-de Haas effect in semiconductors by optical and microwave methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Studies of the dependence of the optical and microwave Shubnikov-de Haas (SdH) effect on magnetic field have been carried out to determine the transport and energetic parameters in semiconductors and systems such InSb, GaAs/Al/sub x/Ga/sub 1-x/As in the observation of this effect in the reflectivity and transmission of the probing radiation.

articleTitle: The effect of thermal annealing on the properties of polysilicon piezoresistors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Polycrystalline silicon offers promise as a pressure sensor material, especially for extended temperature range applications. The investigation of the dependencies of polysilicon layers' physical properties on deposition and annealing parameters is the aim of this work.

articleTitle: Cold cathode based on a formed metal-insulator-metal structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Hybrid vacuum integrated circuits operating in the UHF range is one application where cold cathodes with high current density are needed. The cold cathode based on the formed metal-insulator-metal (MIM) structure is a kind of field emitter and it can be potentially used for some UHF applications. Formed MIM cathodes have demonstrated current densities up to 0.5 A/cm/sup 2/, but these values are low and have to be improved. Forming is the final step of MIM cathode fabrication strongly affecting its emission characteristics. Despite the fact that numerous work has been done in this field, many aspects of the forming process still remain unclear. The present paper reports some new results on studying the forming process in MIM systems.

articleTitle: Methods of noise protection in laser ranging systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The engineering process of laser ranging systems (LRS) is connected to intensive analysis of statistical properties of reflected noise of a signal in the optical range. In the given article attention to the analysis of pattern noise of a signal reflected from aerosol environment and detection of the tags obtained is given at the expense of a change of parameters of a system ensuring a noise immunity LRS.

articleTitle: Optimization of noise performance for three first-order microwave active recursive filters topologies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In this article, three topologies of microwave active recursive filters are studied. We show how, using a noise wave formalism, the noise factor of active recursive filters can be effectively minimized. A comparison between the different topologies is given. Simulations and practical results are also presented to validate our approach.

articleTitle: The numerical simulation of the heat-transfer processes in the silicon heat flow sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The authors use finite element analysis to model two types of Si heat flow sensors, i.e. membrane- and plate-type sensors. Numerical simulation of heat transfer processes in the sensors is performed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic microwave systems for safety of mobile link
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The problem of effect on an environment of an electromagnetic radiation (EMR) modern mobile radio systems (MRS) is investigated by using as theoretical (probability simulation of ecological risk), and experimental (monitoring under the factor of EMR) methods. The results of that research is being discussed front the point of view of safety parameters under the factor EMR MRS of the GSM standard a Ltd. "SMARTS" (Samara).

articleTitle: The model of varactor for the analysis of a multiplier of frequency in the time domain
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: A model of a multiplier microwave diode is considered which is received on the basis of updating of Agahanyn's model for a bipolar transistor. The model consists of a linear and nonlinear part, that simplifies its use on the analysis of varactor multiplier of frequency in the time area.

articleTitle: Physical modelling of space charge waves in relativistic electron beams
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Studying of space charge waves (SCW) is important both for optimisation of multi-cavity relativistic klystrons (MRK) and for their usage in wave methods of collective ion acceleration. In both these cases should be known plasma wavelength, its dependence from the amplitude of the signal exciting the SCW. Calculation of this characteristic of SCW on the basis of different models, especially in nonlinear regime, is not exact. That is why physical experiment is important, which lets to define plasma wavelength in linear and nonlinear regimes. In this connection the task of operative physical modelling of SCW in relativistic electron beams and the study of their characteristics in nonlinear model is of actuality.

articleTitle: The research of performances of the generator on the tunnel diode at the influence of an external microwave signal
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In this work the results of a computer simulation of the performance of a tunnel diode (TD) generator under the influence of an external microwave signal taking into consideration the change of the TD I-V characteristics because of the heating of the free charge carriers are presented.

articleTitle: Measurements of electromagnetic properties of dielectric materials in the microwave range
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In this work the theory, analysis and a practical implementation of a method of measurement of relative dielectric permeability /spl epsiv/*=/spl epsi/-i/spl middot//spl epsiv/" of materials in a frequency range from 0.5 up to 25 GHz is considered. Values of /spl epsi/ were measured in a range from 2 up to 200 relative units and values of dielectric losses tg/spl delta/ (/spl epsiv/"//spl epsi/) in a range from 5/spl middot/10/sup -5/ up to 2/spl middot/10/sup -2/.

articleTitle: Some aspects of a rf plasma reactor design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: At construction of RF plasma generators there is a need for sources of RF power capable to work in polyharmonic mode and permitting to execute distributed input of energy to a reactor volume. It is offered to use a modified discrete distributed amplifier (DDA) as a power source for the extended RF capacitively coupled low-temperature plasma generator. The load, which one is a plasma reactor, directly enters in a load line (LL) being by its a design part. Thus, the load is distributed lengthways of LL, instead of is massed on the end, as in the original DDA circuit. Last constrains us to revise processes flowing past in LL completely and look on efficiency of DDA in a new fashion.

articleTitle: Quasistatic large signal model of transistors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The approach to the build-up of quasistatic large signal model of two-ports is offered. In this approach small single-tone signal with constant bias is used. A quasistatic large signal model of transistor is proposed.

articleTitle: The dynamical spread Talyrond trace model of the surface for investigation of endurance of the component
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: In given work dynamic distributed model is offered for detail wear process description in good time and on the length of rotation. Building of dynamic model with distributed parameters is based on detail surface picture reconstruction in fixed moments of the time, i.e. N profilogram building in the statics for moments of the time t/sub 0/, t/sub 1/, ..., t/sub N/. Besides static distributed type model describes surface structure on the whole detail length and generates original data for dynamic model reconstruction. The wear process dynamics in good time for fixed points on the detail length is described by means of stochastic distributed type model in the state-space.

articleTitle: Design of matching networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The design of matching network is the task that engineer very often meets in his practice. A large number of work is devoted to this problem but it is still remained actual. It is connected with fact that the classical theory of broadband matching of Bode-Fano-Youla do not permit to take into account a lot of restrictions which are met at practical application of radioelectronic devices. Moreover, this theory generally yields suboptimal results and it is applied only for relatively simple load structure. However, the analytic theory is fundamental importance for understanding matching problems. The main numerical methods are considered in the present work. A brief description of operation and comparative characteristics are given.

articleTitle: Proof of a relation between phasors of certain harmonic components of memoryless amplifier output signal
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: It is shown that there holds a relation between the phasors of fundamental components, in the input and output signals, and the phasors of the third order intermodulation (IMD3) components of the output signal, when a sum of a two-tone signal and a signal consisting of components at difference mixing frequencies is sent through a nonlinear memoryless amplifier. This relation can result in an interesting effect. In the output signal, simultaneously the IMD3 products are cancelled and the ratio of the phasors of fundamental components is restored.

articleTitle: On applications of active filters for reduction of nonlinear distortions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: Study efficiency of out-of-band correction of intermodulation distortions for power transistor RF amplifiers for the two variants of realization of out-of-band correction elements (with help of elementary physically realizable passive circuits and with help of active filters). It is shown that the correction by means of passive circuits allow to get scoring on reduction of IMD/sub 3/ up to 10...13 dB, whereas the correction by means of active filters allow to get scoring up to 25 dB.

articleTitle: The critical concentrations of the substituting metal on the phase diagram La/sub 2-x/(Ca,Sr,Ba)/sub x/CuO/sub 4/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: The results of critical concentration calculations of the high T/sub c/ compound La/sub 2-x/(Ca,Sr,Ba)/sub x/CuO/sub 4/ are presented. The calculation was obtained by the analysis of the location model of the substituting metal in the crystal structure of this compound.

articleTitle: Numerical methods for computation of microwave devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the IEEE - Russia Conference. 1999 High Power Microwave Electronics: Measurements, Identification, Applications. MIA-ME'99 (Cat. No.99EX289)
abstract: A large number of methods for calculation of electromagnetic fields in the microwave devices, developed to the present time, testifies that the method, which suits for the solution of most problem meeting in practice, at the given moment does not exist. In this connection the comparative characteristic, which would allow to make a well-grounded choice for the solving given class of problems, has the important meaning. Such characteristic should emanate from the certain criterions. The degree of correspondence to these criterions defines the position of given method among others.
